summary: Maven/Guice [GAP: Agent bootstrap and Kafka trace continuity] -> orders -> parser [GAP: Silent parse drops] -> enrichment -> orders.enriched and conditional orders.fraud-alerts; stream lifecycle [GAP: Stream lifecycle visibility]; native client metric samples [GAP: Consumer lag visibility].

evidence.finding: Maven module with Kafka Streams, Guice, Jackson and slf4j-simple; no active OTel setup.
Main creates the Guice service, registers close on shutdown, starts the stream and joins.
No HTTP routes; one input and two output topic paths are defined by the topology.
Maven exec runs the main class; the service owns the KafkaStreams instance and its existing handler/close behavior.

findings.title: Trace orders through Kafka Streams
findings.area: Agent bootstrap and Kafka trace continuity
findings.gap: No Java agent, OTel dependencies/provider, propagation setup, exporter or resource setup exists in the runnable service. Kafka input processing and both output topics have no OTel coverage; source logs alone cannot localize broker/processor failures.
findings.impact: Operators cannot follow a delayed or failed order across the processor and its output topics or associate a fault with the running release.
findings.product_outcome: Operators should see a Kafka processing waterfall, both output destinations, and JVM capacity charts for the same service.
findings.required_fix: Use the standard Java-agent path for Kafka traces and metrics with one provider owner, preserved topology/Guice structure, configured resources and transport, and observed shutdown behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Use the standard Java-agent path for Kafka traces and metrics with one provider owner, preserved topology/Guice structure, configured resources and transport, and observed shutdown behavior.
constraints: Preserve existing business behavior and telemetry ownership; keep private data and unbounded identities out of telemetry dimensions.
Preserve the documented Maven runner, existing logging and one agent-owned provider; no second SDK or Guice Tracer binding.

expected_telemetry.name: Kafka client and stream operations
expected_telemetry.product_view: Operators should see a Kafka processing waterfall, both output destinations, and JVM capacity charts for the same service.

findings.title: Make silent record drops visible
findings.gap: OrderEventParser.parse returns Optional.empty for null payloads and JsonProcessingException; flatMapValues removes them without any telemetry. An agent process span may complete successfully for these handled drops. toJson throws and is not a silent-drop gap.
findings.impact: Bad input can disappear while the consumer appears healthy, making data loss difficult to detect or quantify.
findings.product_outcome: Operators should see a chart of intentionally dropped records by a bounded parse reason.
findings.required_fix: Bounded app-owned metrics distinguish successful processing from handled null/malformed parse drops without changing parser returns or output routing.
acceptance_criteria: Bounded app-owned metrics distinguish successful processing from handled null/malformed parse drops without changing parser returns or output routing.
constraints: Preserve existing business behavior and telemetry ownership; keep private data and unbounded identities out of telemetry dimensions.
A JSON literal null is distinct from a null payload: preserve the source's uncaught failure rather than reclassifying it as a handled parse drop.

expected_telemetry.name: Record processing and handled-drop outcomes
expected_telemetry.product_view: Operators should see a chart of intentionally dropped records by a bounded parse reason.

follow_up_actions: Select this finding in otel.html and use the bundled instrumentation handoff.

findings.title: Detect a stopped stream in a live JVM
findings.gap: The uncaught handler requests SHUTDOWN_CLIENT, but main joins indefinitely. No observable stream state or failure metric exists. The started/stopped logs are asynchronous/unchecked status hints, and jvm uptime does not prove Kafka processing readiness.
findings.impact: A process-level health check can stay green after stream threads have stopped processing orders.
findings.product_outcome: Operators should see the current stream state and a failure count even when the JVM remains alive.
findings.required_fix: Bounded failure/lifecycle telemetry distinguishes a stopped stream from a live JVM while preserving the existing handler response and close ownership.
acceptance_criteria: Bounded failure/lifecycle telemetry distinguishes a stopped stream from a live JVM while preserving the existing handler response and close ownership.
constraints: Preserve existing business behavior and telemetry ownership; keep private data and unbounded identities out of telemetry dimensions.
Do not change SHUTDOWN_CLIENT, main-thread joining, shutdown timeout, liveness policy or fixed native log messages.

expected_telemetry.name: Stream lifecycle and processing failure outcomes
expected_telemetry.product_view: Operators should see the current stream state and a failure count even when the JVM remains alive.

follow_up_actions: Select this finding in otel.html and use the bundled instrumentation handoff.

findings.title: Expose consumer backlog
findings.gap: The service owns Kafka consumers, but no OTel bridge exports their native lag samples. Kafka process spans and JVM memory do not measure backlog. Records contain no event timestamp or expected cadence to justify an event-freshness gauge.
findings.impact: Operators cannot distinguish a healthy idle service from input accumulating faster than the processor can drain it.
findings.product_outcome: Operators should see a consumer-lag chart that rises under backlog and falls as processing catches up.
findings.required_fix: Expose the maximum valid app-visible records-lag-max sample, in records, from the owned native clients; absent, NaN or negative samples remain unavailable instead of becoming a synthetic healthy zero.
acceptance_criteria: Expose the maximum valid app-visible records-lag-max sample, in records, from the owned native clients; absent, NaN or negative samples remain unavailable instead of becoming a synthetic healthy zero.
constraints: Preserve existing business behavior and telemetry ownership; keep private data and unbounded identities out of telemetry dimensions.

Use only KafkaStreams.metrics() samples exposed by the owned client; records-lag-max is not total broker backlog, topic availability or event-time freshness. Preserve native values, one measurement owner and bounded series.

expected_telemetry.name: Application-visible consumer lag
expected_telemetry.product_view: Operators should see a consumer-lag chart that rises under backlog and falls as processing catches up.
